I am 70 this year, and I have worked these 2.6 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. Me and my old woman manage it ourselves. I only went to primary school, so I do not read books about farming. I learned by watching my father and by copying what works in the village. Old Wang across the road has good wheat every year, so I use the same improved wheat seed he buys from the shop. Last year my wheat gave about 480 jin per mu and my maize gave about 580 jin per mu, so I will do almost the same thing this year. Change is risky.

For my wheat, I sowed it last October after running the rotary tiller twice to break up the wheat stubble from the previous summer. At sowing I put down one bag — 50 kilograms — of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer for each mu. That is my base. When it turned green this March, I spread another 15 kilograms of urea per mu. Now it is April and the wheat is jointing, so I will irrigate once now and spread 10 more kilograms of urea per mu. I irrigate four times in total: once before winter, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice — once for weeds and once for aphids or rust if I see it. I do not dare cut back on fertilizer. One bag of compound and 25 kilograms of urea per mu costs me real money, maybe 200 yuan per mu, but if I use less and the yield drops, I lose far more. A bad harvest means no money for medicine.

For my maize, after I harvest the wheat in early June, I plant hybrid maize seed right away using the no-tillage seeder. Time is short and I am old, so I do not plough for maize. I put 40 kilograms of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu at sowing. When the maize reaches big trumpet stage, I topdress with 20 kilograms of urea per mu and irrigate. I irrigate twice for maize if the rain does not come — once at jointing and once at filling. I spray herbicide once after sowing and insecticide once when I see worms. I expect about 580 kilograms per mu if the weather is normal.

My land is small, so every jin of fertilizer and every yuan matters. But I would rather put a little too much than too little. The neighbors around me do about the same, so I sleep better knowing I am not taking chances.
